351.subject: Botany
351.text: Which of the following features can be said to be a true defining feature of living beings without any exception?
options: They can respond to external stimuli.
351.sol: The most obvious and technically complicated feature of all living organisms is their ability to sense their surroundings or environment and respond to these environmental stimuli which could be physical, chemical or biological. All organisms, from the prokaryotes to the most complex eukaryotes can sense and respond to environmental cues eg. Photoperiod affects reproduction in seasonal breeders, both plants and animals. Consciousness therefore, becomes the defining property of living organisms. There are many organisms which do not reproduce e.g. mule. Thus, reproduction cannot be an all-inclusive defining characteristic of living organisms. However no non-living object is capable of reproducing or replicating by itself.

1364.text: As shown in figure, two vertical conducting rails separated by distance $1.0 \mathrm{~m}$ are placed parallel to $z$-axis. 1364.sol:
Due to motion of rod, emf induced across capacitor, $\varepsilon=B l v \therefore \quad$ Charge stored in capacitor, $Q=C(B l v) I=\frac{d Q}{d t}=C B l \frac{d v}{d t}=C B l a$
Force opposing the downward motion, $F_m=B I l \therefore \quad F_m=B(C B l a) l=B^2 l^2 C a$
Net force on rod, $F_{\text{net }}=W-F_m=m g-B^2 l^2 C a \therefore \quad m a=m g-B^2 l^2 C a$
or $\quad a=\frac{m g}{\left(m+B^2 l^2 C\right)}$
So, $\quad a=\frac{0.1 \times 9.8}{\left(0.1+2^2 \times 1^2 \times 0.15\right)}=1.4 \mathrm{ m} / $$\mathrm{s}^2$

options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion

2008.sol: Adrenaline is a catecholamine hormone, also known as epinephrine, secreted by the mammalian adrenal medulla as well as the adrenergic nerve endings. It also raises metabolic rate.

2227.text:
Assertion : Mullerian and Batesian mimicry both are protective mimicry.
Reason : Viceroy butterfly shows Mullerian mimicry.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
2227.sol: Defensive or protective mimicry takes place when organisms are able to avoid harmful encounters by deceiving enemies into treating them as something else. In Batesian mimicry, a harmless species poses as harmful to deceive predator. In Mullerian mimicry, two or more harmful species mutually advertise themselves as harmful for their mutual benifit. Viceroy butterfly mimics unpalatable toxic Monarch butterfly, thus, shows Batesian mimicry.

& \text{ Increased pressure }=\frac{a}{\frac{199}{200} V^{1 / 4}}=\frac{200 a}{199 V^{1 / 4}}
\end{aligned}\therefore$ Percentage increase in pressure $\begin{aligned}& =\frac{\frac{200 a}{199 V^{1 / 4}}-\frac{a}{V^{1 / 4}}}{\frac{a}{V^{1 / 4}}} \times100 \\
& =\left(\frac{200}{199}-1\right) \times100 \\
& =\frac{100}{199} \approx \frac{1}{2}(\text{ approximate })
\end{aligned}$

8234.text: $The solution of \left(1+x^2\right) \frac{d y}{d x}+2 x y-4 x^2=0$ is :
8234.sol:
$\left(1+x^2\right) \frac{d y}{d x}+2 x y-4 x^2=0\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d y}{d x}+\left(\frac{2 x}{1+x^2}\right) y=\frac{4 x^2}{1+x^2}$
On comparing with $\frac{d y}{d x}+P y=Q$, we get
$P=\frac{2 x}{1+x^2}, Q=\frac{4 x^2}{1+x^2}$
I.F. $=e^{\int P d x}=e^{\log \left(1+x^2\right)}=1+x^2$
The solution is
$y \text{ (I.F.) }=\int Q \text{ (I. F. ) } d x+c_1\Rightarrow \quad y\left(1+x^2\right)=\int \frac{4 x^2}{\left(1+x^2\right)}\left(1+x^2\right) d x+C_1\Rightarrow \quad y\left(1+x^2\right)=\frac{4 x^3}{3}+c_1\Rightarrow \quad 3 y\left(1+x^2\right)=4 x^3+c$

10366.text: If $8 \cdot{ }^7 P_r=7 \cdot{ }^8 P_{r-1}$, what is the value of $r$ ?
10366.sol:
$8 \cdot{ }^7 P_r=7 \cdot{ }^8 P_{r-1}\begin{aligned} & 8 \cdot \frac{7 !}{(7-r) !}=7 \cdot \frac{8 !}{\{8-(r-1)\} !} \\ & \frac{8 !}{(7-r) !}=\frac{7 \cdot 8 !}{(9-r) !} \\ & \frac{1}{(7-r) !}=\frac{7}{(9-r)(8-r)\{(7-r) !\}} \\ & 1=\frac{7}{72-9 r-8 r+r^2} \\ & r^2-17 r+72-7=0 \\ & r^2-17 r+65=0 \\ & r=\frac{17 \pm \sqrt{(17)^2-4 \times 65}}{2}\end{aligned}$
which is not a natural number.

18062.text: If $\left(1 + x + x^{2}\right)20 = \mathop{∑}_{r = 0}^{40}{a}_{r} \cdot x^{r}$, then $\mathop{∑}_{r = 0}^{39}\left(- 1\right)r \cdot {a}_{r} \cdot {a}_{r + 1}$& equal to
18062.sol:
We have, $\left(1 + x + x^{2}\right)20 = \mathop{∑}_{r = 0}^{40}{a}_{r}x^{r}$

$x$ is replaced by $- \dfrac{1}{x}$, we get

$\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{x} + \dfrac{1}{x2}\right)20 = \mathop{∑}_{r = 0}^{40} ( - 1{)}^{r}{a}_{r}\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)r$

$\left(1 - x + x^{2}\right)20 = \mathop{∑}_{r = 0}^{40} ( - 1{)}^{r}{a}_{r}x^{40 - r}$

$\mathop{∑}_{r = 0}^{39}\left(- 1\right)r{a}_{r} \cdot {a}_{r + 1}$ is coefficient of $x$ in product of~$\left(1 + x + x^{2}\right)20\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{x} + \dfrac{1}{x2}\right)20$

Now,~$\left(1 + x + x^{2}\right)20\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{x} + \dfrac{1}{x2}\right)20 = \left(1 + x^{2} + \dfrac{1}{x2}\right)20$

19607.subject: Chemistry
19607.text: An optically active compound $[\mathrm{X}]$ (Molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_8 \mathrm{H}_{11} \mathrm{ N}$ ) reacts with $\mathrm{CHCl}_3$ / Ethanolic KOH on heating to form an isocyanide. On reaction with $\mathrm{NaNO}_2 / \mathrm{HCl}$, it yields an alcohol with liberation of $\mathrm{N}_2$. Identify the compound $[\mathrm{X}]$.
19607.sol:
The molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_8 \mathrm{H}_{11} \mathrm{N}$ corresponds to a degree of unsaturation of $8 - \dfrac{11}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} + 1 = 4$. This indicates the presence of a benzene ring.

The reaction with $\mathrm{CHCl}_3 / \mathrm{KOH}$ (carbylamine test) indicates that $[\mathrm{X}]$ is a primary amine. The reaction with $\mathrm{NaNO}_2 / \mathrm{HCl}$ yielding an alcohol with the liberation of $\mathrm{N}_2$ is characteristic of aliphatic primary amines, as aromatic primary amines form diazonium salts which are stable at low temperatures.

Among the options, 1-phenylethanamine ($\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{NH}_2) \mathrm{CH}_3$) is a primary amine where the amino group is attached to an aliphatic carbon. It contains a chiral center at the carbon atom attached to the amino group, making it optically active. The other options are aromatic amines (anilines), which do not form alcohols under these conditions but rather form stable diazonium salts at $0-5^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$.

Therefore, 1-phenylethanamine satisfies all the given conditions.

Answer: 1-Phenylethanamine.

19657.subject: Chemistry
19657.text: Which statement is incorrect about aminoacids?
options: $\alpha$-aminoacids are soluble in polar solvents like petroleum ether and benzene.
All aminoacids except glycine are optically active.
At isoelectric point, an aminoacid has the least solubility in water.
19657.sol:
Amino acids are polar compounds due to the presence of both amino and carboxyl groups, which exist as zwitterions in aqueous solutions. Because of their ionic nature, they are highly soluble in water but are insoluble in non-polar organic solvents like petroleum ether and benzene.

Methionine is indeed an essential amino acid, meaning it cannot be synthesized by the human body and must be obtained through diet.

Glycine is the simplest amino acid with the structure $NH_2-CH_2-COOH$. Since the $\alpha$-carbon is attached to two identical hydrogen atoms, it is achiral and thus optically inactive. All other naturally occurring $\alpha$-amino acids possess a chiral $\alpha$-carbon and are optically active.

At the isoelectric point, the net charge on the amino acid is zero. In this state, the electrostatic attractions between the zwitterions are maximized, and the interaction with water molecules is minimized, leading to the lowest solubility in water.

Therefore, the statement that $\alpha$-amino acids are soluble in non-polar solvents like petroleum ether and benzene is incorrect.

Answer: $\alpha$-aminoacids are soluble in polar solvents like petroleum ether and benzene.

19981.subject: Chemistry
19981.text: The number of geometrical isomers in the following metal complexes $\mathrm{Ni}$($\mathrm{CO}$)_4,$\left[\mathrm{Ru}\left(\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}\right)_3\mathrm{Cl}_{3}\right],\left[\mathrm{CuCl}_{2}  \left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_4\right]^{+}and \left[\m$ mathrm{PtCl}_2$\left(\mathrm{NH}_{3}\right)_2\right] are$
19981.sol:
The complex $\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_4$ is a tetrahedral complex of the type $MA_4$. Tetrahedral complexes of the type $MA_4$ or $MA_3B$ do not exhibit geometrical isomerism. Thus, the number of geometrical isomers is $0$.

The complex $[\mathrm{Ru}(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O})_3\mathrm{Cl}_3]$ is an octahedral complex of the type $MA_3B_3$. This type of complex exhibits two geometrical isomers: the facial (fac) isomer and the meridional (mer) isomer. Thus, the number of geometrical isomers is $2$.

The complex $[\mathrm{CuCl}_2(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4]^{+}$ is an octahedral complex of the type $MA_4B_2$. This type of complex exhibits two geometrical isomers: the trans isomer (where the two Cl ligands are at $180^{{}^{\circ}}$) and the cis isomer (where the two Cl ligands are at $90^{{}^{\circ}}$). Thus, the number of geometrical isomers is $2$.

The complex $[\mathrm{PtCl}_2(\mathrm{NH}_3)_2]$ is a square planar complex of the type $MA_2B_2$. This type of complex exhibits two geometrical isomers: the cis isomer and the trans isomer. Thus, the number of geometrical isomers is $2$.

The sequence of the number of geometrical isomers is $0, 2, 2, 2$.

Answer: $0,2,2,2$

21318.subject: Mathematics
21318.text: The solution of $dy = \cos x (2 - y \ \text{cosec} \ x) dx$ where $y = \sqrt{2}$ when $x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ is
21318.sol:
The given differential equation can be rewritten as:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2\cos x - y \cos x \text{cosec} x$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y \cot x = 2\cos x$

This is a linear differential equation of the form $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + P y = Q$, where $P = \cot x$ and $Q = 2\cos x$.

The integrating factor (IF) is:

$\text{IF} = e^{\int \cot x dx} = e^{\ln(\sin x)} = \sin x$

Multiplying the differential equation by the integrating factor and integrating both sides:

$y \sin x = \int 2\sin x \cos x dx + C$

$y \sin x = \int \sin 2x dx + C$

$y \sin x = -\dfrac{\cos 2x}{2} + C$

Given $y = \sqrt{2}$ when $x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$:

$\sqrt{2} \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = -\dfrac{\cos(\pi/2)}{2} + C$

$\sqrt{2} \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = 0 + C \Rightarrow C = 1$

Substituting $C = 1$ back into the equation:

$y \sin x = 1 - \dfrac{\cos 2x}{2}$

$y \sin x = 1 - \dfrac{1 - 2\sin^2 x}{2}$

$y \sin x = \dfrac{1}{2} + \sin^2 x$

$y = \dfrac{1}{2\sin x} + \sin x$

$y = \sin x + \dfrac{1}{2} \text{cosec} x$

21610.subject: Mathematics
21610.text: Given $\cos \left(\tan ^{-1}x\right)=\sin \left(\cot ^{-1} \dfrac{3}{4}\right), then the value of $ x$ is$
21610.sol:
Let $\theta = \tan^{-1} x$. Then $\tan \theta = x$. Since $\cos \theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 + \tan^2 \theta}}$, we have $\cos(\tan^{-1} x) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 + x^2}}$.

Let $\phi = \cot^{-1} \dfrac{3}{4}$. Then $\cot \phi = \dfrac{3}{4}$, which implies $\tan \phi = \dfrac{4}{3}$.

Using the identity $\sin \phi = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 + \cot^2 \phi}}$, we have $\sin(\cot^{-1} \dfrac{3}{4}) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 + (3/4)^2}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 + 9/16}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{25/16}} = \dfrac{4}{5}$.

Equating the two expressions: $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 + x^2}} = \dfrac{4}{5}$.

Squaring both sides: $\dfrac{1}{1 + x^2} = \dfrac{16}{25}$.

Thus, $1 + x^2 = \dfrac{25}{16}$, which gives $x^2 = \dfrac{25}{16} - 1 = \dfrac{9}{16}$.

Taking the square root, $x = \dfrac{3}{4}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{3}{4}$

23321.subject: Physics
23321.text: A particle executes a simple harmonic motion of amplitude $\mathrm{A}$. The distance from the mean position at which its kinetic energy is equal to its potential energy is
23321.sol:
The kinetic energy $K$ and potential energy $U$ of a particle executing simple harmonic motion with amplitude $A$ at a distance $x$ from the mean position are given by $K = \dfrac{1}{2} k(A^2 - x^2)$ and $U = \dfrac{1}{2} k x^2$, where $k$ is the force constant.

Given that the kinetic energy is equal to the potential energy, we set $K = U$:

$\dfrac{1}{2} k(A^2 - x^2) = \dfrac{1}{2} k x^2$

Simplifying the equation:

$A^2 - x^2 = x^2$

$A^2 = 2x^2$

$x^2 = \dfrac{A^2}{2}$

$x = \dfrac{A}{\sqrt{2}}$

Using the value $\sqrt{2} \approx 1.414$, we calculate:

$x = \dfrac{A}{1.414} \approx 0.707 A$

Rounding to two decimal places, we get $x = 0.71 A$.

Answer: 0.71 A

23373.subject: Physics
23373.text: A ray of light travelling through a medium of refractive index $\dfrac{5}{4}$ is incident on a glass of refractive index $\dfrac{3}{2}$. Find the angle of refraction in the glass, if the angle of incidence at the given medium - glass interface is $30^{\circ}$.
23373.sol:
Given the refractive index of the first medium $n_1 = \dfrac{5}{4}$ and the refractive index of the second medium (glass) $n_2 = \dfrac{3}{2}$.

The angle of incidence $i = 30^{\circ}$.

Using Snell's Law, $n_1 \sin(i) = n_2 \sin(r)$, where $r$ is the angle of refraction.

Substituting the given values:

$\dfrac{5}{4} \sin(30^{\circ}) = \dfrac{3}{2} \sin(r)$

Since $\sin(30^{\circ}) = \dfrac{1}{2}$, we have:

$\dfrac{5}{4} \times \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{3}{2} \sin(r)$

$\dfrac{5}{8} = \dfrac{3}{2} \sin(r)$

$\sin(r) = \dfrac{5}{8} \times \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{10}{24} = \dfrac{5}{12}$

Therefore, $r = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{5}{12}\right)$.

Answer: $\sin ^{-1}\left(\dfrac{5}{12}\right)$

24240.subject: Mathematics
24240.text: Consider the points $A(4\hat{i} + \hat{j} + 3\hat{k})$, $B(2\hat{j})$ and $C(-4\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 3\hat{k})$. Which of the following statements is TRUE?
24240.sol:
Position vectors of the points are given as $\vec{A} = 4\hat{i} + \hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$, $\vec{B} = 2\hat{j}$, and $\vec{C} = -4\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}$.

The vectors $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{BC}$ are calculated as follows:

$\overrightarrow{AB} = \vec{B} - \vec{A} = (0 - 4)\hat{i} + (2 - 1)\hat{j} + (0 - 3)\hat{k} = -4\hat{i} + \hat{j} - 3\hat{k}$

$\overrightarrow{BC} = \vec{C} - \vec{B} = (-4 - 0)\hat{i} + (3 - 2)\hat{j} + (-3 - 0)\hat{k} = -4\hat{i} + \hat{j} - 3\hat{k}$

Since $\overrightarrow{AB} = \overrightarrow{BC}$, the vectors are parallel and share the common point $B$.

Therefore, the points $A$, $B$, and $C$ are collinear.

Answer: $A$, $B$ and $C$ are collinear.

25955.text: Let $a, b, c$ be three non-zero real numbers such that the equation $\sqrt{3}acos ⁡ x + 2bsin ⁡ x = c, x \in \left[- \dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$ has two distinct real roots $\alpha$ and $\beta$ with $\alpha + \beta = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$. Then, the value of $\dfrac{b}{a}$ is
25955.sol:
$\sqrt{3}cos ⁡ x + \dfrac{2b}{a}sin ⁡ x = \dfrac{c}{a}$
Now, $\sqrt{3}cos ⁡ \alpha + \dfrac{2b}{a}sin ⁡ \alpha = \dfrac{c}{a} \ldots \left(i\right)
$\sqrt{3}cos ⁡ \beta + $\dfrac{2b}{a}$sin ⁡ \beta = $\dfrac{c}{a}$ \ldots $\left(ii\right)$

From equations $\left(i\right)$ and $\left(ii\right)$

$⇒ \sqrt{3}\left[cos ⁡ \alpha - cos ⁡ \beta\right] + \dfrac{2b}{a}\left(sin ⁡ \alpha - sin ⁡ \beta\right) = 0$
$⇒ \sqrt{3}\left[- 2sin ⁡ \left(\dfrac{\alpha + \beta}{2}\right)sin ⁡ \left(\dfrac{\alpha - \beta}{2}\right)\right] + \dfrac{2b}{a}\left[2cos ⁡ \left(\dfrac{\alpha + \beta}{2}\right)sin ⁡ \left(\dfrac{\alpha - \beta}{2}\right)\right] = 0$

$⇒ - \sqrt{3} + 2\sqrt{3} \cdot \dfrac{b}{a} = 0$
$⇒ \dfrac{b}{a} = \dfrac{1}{2} = 0.5$

26433.text: A ball is thrown from ground at an angle $\theta$ with horizontal and with an initial speed ${u}_{0} .$ For the resulting projectile motion, the magnitude of average velocity of the ball up to the point when it hits the ground for the first time is ${V}_{1} .$ After hitting the ground, ball rebounds at the same angle $\theta$ but with a reduced speed of $\dfrac{{u}_{0}}{\alpha} .$ Its motion continues for a long time as shown in figure. If the magnitude of average velocity of the ball for entire duration of motion is $0.8{V}_{1},$ the value of $\alpha$ is______
26433.sol:
For first projectile
Average velocity, $\left(V\right) = \dfrac{R}{T} = {U}_{x} = {V}_{1}\left(\begin{array}{ll}\left(whereR = RangeandT = Timeofflight\right) \\ R = \dfrac{2{U}_{x} . {U}_{y}}{g} T = \dfrac{2 . {U}_{y}}{g}\end{array}\right)$
For journey
${\left(V\right)}_{1 \to n} = \dfrac{{R}_{1} + {R}_{2} + \ldots + {R}_{n}}{{T}_{1} + {T}_{2} + \ldots + {T}_{n}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{2{u}_{{x}_{1}}{u}_{{y}_{1}}}{g} + \dfrac{2{u}_{{x}_{2}}{u}_{{y}_{2}}}{g} + \ldots + \dfrac{2{u}_{{x}_{n}}{u}_{{y}_{n}}}{g}}{\dfrac{2{u}_{{y}_{1}}}{g} + \dfrac{2{u}_{{y}_{2}}}{g} + \ldots \dfrac{2{u}_{{y}_{n}}}{g}}$
$⇒ {U}_{x}\left(\dfrac{1 + \dfrac{1}{{\alpha}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{{\alpha}^{4}} + \ldots \dfrac{1}{{\alpha}^{2n}}}{1 + \dfrac{1}{\alpha} + \dfrac{1}{{\alpha}^{2}} + \ldots + \dfrac{1}{{\alpha}^{n}}}\right) = 0.8{v}_{1}, \left(\begin{array}{ll}1 + \dfrac{1}{{\alpha}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{{\alpha}^{4}} + \ldots \dfrac{1}{{\alpha}^{2n}} ⇒ Geometricprogression \\ SumofG . P . = \dfrac{1}{1 - {\alpha}^{2}}\end{array}\right)$
$⇒ \dfrac{{V}_{1}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 - \dfrac{1}{{\alpha}^{2}}}\right)}{\left(\dfrac{1}{1 - \dfrac{1}{\alpha}}\right)} = 0.8{v}_{1} ⇒ \dfrac{\alpha}{1 + \alpha} = 0.8 ⇒ \alpha = 4$

26572.subject: Physics
26572.text:
Paragraph: The figure shows a surface $X Y$ separating two transparent media, medium-1 and medium-2. The lines $a b$ and $c d$ represent wavefronts of a light wave travelling in medium-1 and incident on $X Y$. The lines ef and $g h$ represent wavefronts of the light wave in medium-2 after refraction.
Question: The phases of the light wave at $c, d, e$ and $f$ are $\phi_c, \phi_d, \phi_e$ and $\phi_f$, respectively. It is given that $\phi_c \neq \phi_f$.
options:
$\phi_c$ cannot be equal to $\phi_d$

$\phi_d$ can be equal to $\phi_e$

$\left(\phi_d-\phi_f\right)$ is equal to $\left(\phi_c-\phi_e\right)$

$\left(\phi_d-\phi_c\right)$ is not equal to $\left(\phi_f-\phi_e\right)$
26572.sol:
All points on a wavefront are at the same phase.
$ \begin{array}{rlrl}
\therefore & \phi_d & =\phi_c \text{ and } \phi_f=\phi_e \\
& \therefore & \phi_d-\phi_f & =\phi_c-\phi_e
\end{array} $
Hence, the correct option is (c).

26676.subject: Physics
26676.text:
Paragraph
A thermally insulating cylinder has a thermally insulating and frictionless movable partition in the middle, as shown in the figure below. On each side of the partition, there is one mole of an ideal gas, with specific heat at constant volume, $C_{V}=2 R$. Here, $R$ is the gas constant. Initially, each side has a volume $V_{0}$ and temperature $T_{0}$. The left side has an electric heater, which is turned on at very low power to transfer heat $Q$ to the gas on the left side. As a result the partition moves slowly towards the right reducing the right side volume to $V_{0} / 2$. Consequently, the gas temperatures on the left and the right sides become $T_{L}$ and $T_{R}$, respectively. Ignore the changes in the temperatures of the cylinder, heater and the partition.

QuestionThe value of $\dfrac{Q}{R{T}_{0}}$ is:
26676.sol:
Writing ${C}_{V}$ in terms of degree of freedom of the gas $f$, we get,

${C}_{V} = \dfrac{f}{2}R = 2R ⇒ f = 4,$

Therefore,​ adiabatic index of gas will be given by,​​​​​​$\gamma = 1 + \dfrac{2}{f} = 1 + \dfrac{2}{4} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

The gas of the right portion has undergone through an adiabatic process so,

${T}_{i}{V}_{i}^{\gamma - 1} = {T}_{f}{V}_{f}^{\gamma - 1} ⇒ {T}_{0}{V}_{0}^{\dfrac{3}{2} - 1} = {T}_{R}{\left(\dfrac{{V}_{0}}{2}\right)}^{\dfrac{3}{2} - 1}$

$⇒ {T}_{R} = \sqrt{2}{T}_{0} ⇒ \dfrac{{T}_{R}}{{T}_{0}} = \sqrt{2}$

Work done by the gas $\left(2\right)$, $= - ∆ U = - n{C}_{V}\left({T}_{f} - {T}_{i}\right)$

$= - \left(1\right)\left(2R\right)\left(\sqrt{2}{T}_{0} - {T}_{0}\right)$

$= - \left(2\sqrt{2} - 2\right)R{T}_{0}$

So work done by the gas $\left(1\right)$,$= + \left(2\sqrt{2} - 2\right)R{T}_{0}$

$PV = nRT ⇒ P ∝ \dfrac{T}{V}$

For gas $\left(2\right),$ $T \to \sqrt{2}$ times of initial value, Volume $\to \dfrac{1}{2}$ times of initial value

So, $P ∝ \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{\dfrac{1}{2}} = 2\sqrt{2}$ times of initial value$⇒ {P}_{f} = 2\sqrt{2}{P}_{0}$

So pressure of the gas $( 1 )$ will also be $2\sqrt{2}$ times and volume of gas $( 1 )$ becomes $\dfrac{3}{2}$ times

$T ∝ PV$

$⇒ T ∝ \left(2\sqrt{2}\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)\right) = 3\sqrt{2}$ times of initial value

${T}_{L} = 3\sqrt{2}{T}_{0}$

$∆ U$ for the left gas $= n{C}_{V}\left({T}_{f} - {T}_{i}\right)$

$= \left(1\right)\left(2R\right)\left(3\sqrt{2}{T}_{0} - {T}_{0}\right) = \left(6\sqrt{2} - 2\right)R{T}_{0}$

Heat given to gas $( 1 )$,

$Q = W + ∆ U$

$= \left(2\sqrt{2} - 2\right)R{T}_{0} + \left(6\sqrt{2} - 2\right)R{T}_{0}$

$= 4{RT}_{0}\left(2\sqrt{2} - 1\right)$

Therefore,

$\dfrac{Q}{R{T}_{0}} = 4\left(2\sqrt{2} - 1\right)$

The decreasing order of hydride affinity for following carbocations is:

The stability of a carbocation increases with the number of alkyl groups attached to the carbon atom, due to the inductive and hyperconjugation effects of the alkyl groups. 30213.subject: Chemistry
30213.text:
As compared with chlorocyclohexane, which of the following statements correctly apply to chlorobenzene?
A. The magnitude of negative charge is more on chlorine atom.
B. The $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{Cl}$ bond has partial double bond character.
C. $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{Cl}$ bond is less polar.
D. $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{Cl}$ bond is longer due to repulsion between delocalised electrons of the aromatic ring and lone pairs of electrons of chlorine.
E. The $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{Cl}$ bond is formed using $\mathrm{sp}^{2}$ hybridised orbital of carbon.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
30213.sol:
Chlorobenzene has Cl attached to an sp² carbon of the benzene ring, while chlorocyclohexane has Cl attached to an sp³ carbon.

Statement B is correct: the C-Cl bond has partial double bond character due to resonance with the aromatic π system, where chlorine's lone pairs interact with the aromatic ring.

Statement C is correct: the C-Cl bond is less polar in chlorobenzene because the resonance contribution reduces the electronegativity difference between C and Cl.

Statement E is correct: the C-Cl bond is formed using sp² hybridized orbital of carbon.

Statement A is incorrect because chlorine carries less negative charge due to resonance donation to the aromatic system.

Statement D is incorrect because the C-Cl bond is actually shorter in chlorobenzene due to partial double bond character, not longer.

The correct statements are B, C, and E only.

32412.text:
Which of the following represents the Freundlich adsorption isotherms?

(A)

(B)

(C)

(D)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
32412.sol:
The equation $\dfrac{x}{m} = {KP}^{1 / n}$ represents Freundlich adsorption isotherm. It is an empirical relationship between the amount of gas adsorbed by a given amount of solid adsorbent surface and pressure of the gas at a particular temperature.

So, Freundlich adsorption isotherm equation is

$\dfrac{x}{m} = {KP}^{1 / n}$

$⇒ log\dfrac{x}{m} = logK + \dfrac{1}{n}logP$

Extent of adsorption $\left(\dfrac{x}{m}\right)$ decreases with increase in temperature.

34373.text: The value of integral $\int_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{3 \pi}{4}} \frac{x}{1+\sin x} d x$ is
34373.sol:
Let $I=\int_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{3 \pi}{4}} \frac{x}{1+\sin x} d x$ also let $K=\frac{x}{1+\sin x}$
Multiplying numerator and denominator by $(1-\sin x)$, we get;
$$
\begin{aligned}
K &=\frac{x(1-\sin x)}{1-(\sin x)^2}=\frac{x(1-\sin x)}{(\cos x)^2} \\
&=x(1-\sin x) \sec ^2 x \\
&=x \sec ^2 x-x \sin x \sec ^2 x=x \sec ^2 x-x \tan \\
x & \sec x
\end{aligned}
$$
Now, $I=\int_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{3 \pi}{4}} x \sec ^2 x d x-\int_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{3 \pi}{4}} x \sec x \tan x d x$
$$
=\left[x \tan x-\int \frac{d x}{d x} \tan x d x\right]_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{3 \pi}{4}}-\left[x \sec x-\int \frac{d x}{d x} \sec x d x\right]_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{3 \pi}{4}}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
&=[x \tan x-\ln |\sec x|]_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{3 \pi}{4}} \\
&-[x \sec x-\ln |\sec x+\tan x|]_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{3 \pi}{4}}+c \\
&\Rightarrow I=\left\{\left[\frac{3 \pi}{4} \tan \frac{3 \pi}{4}-\ln \left|\frac{3 \pi}{4}\right|\right.\right. \\
&\left.-\left[\frac{3 \pi}{4} \sec \frac{3 \pi}{4}-\ln \left|\sec \frac{3 \pi}{4}+\tan \frac{3 \pi}{4}\right|\right]\right\} \\
&-\left\{\left[\frac{\pi}{4} \tan \frac{\pi}{4}-\ln \left|\frac{\pi}{4}\right|\right.\right. \\
&\left.-\left[\frac{\pi}{4} \sec \frac{\pi}{4}-\ln \left|\sec \frac{\pi}{4}+\tan \frac{\pi}{4}\right|\right]\right\} \\
&=\frac{\pi}{2}(\sqrt{2}+1)
\end{aligned}
$$

34787.subject: Mathematics
34787.text: Let $y = y\left(x\right)$ be the solution of the differential equation ${cosec}^{2}xdy + 2dx = \left(1 + ycos2x\right){cosec}^{2}xdx,$ with $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = 0 .$ Then, the value of ${\left(y\left(0\right) + 1\right)}^{2}$ is equal to:
34787.sol:
Given, ${cosec}^{2}xdy + 2dx = \left(1 + ycos2x\right){cosec}^{2}xdx$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{\sin^{2}x} + 2dx = \left(\dfrac{1 + ycos2x}{\sin^{2}x}\right)dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2\sin^{2}x = 1 + ycos2x$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2\sin^{2}x - 1 = ycos2x$

Using, $cos2x = 1 - 2\sin^{2}x,$ we get

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(- cos2x\right) = ycos2x$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(- cos2x\right)y = cos2x$

This is a linear differential equation of the type $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q,$ where $P \text{ and } Q$ are the functions of $x$ or constants.

Thus, $P = - cos2x \text{ and } Q = cos2x$

Now, we have integrating factor I.F.$= {e}^{∫ Pdx} = {e}^{∫ - cos2xdx} = {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)}$

And, the solution of the given differential equation is

$y\left(I . F .\right) = ∫ Q\left(I . F .\right)dx + c$

$⇒ y \cdot {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)} = ∫ \left(cos2x\right) \cdot {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)}dx + c$

Put $\dfrac{sin2x}{2} = t, ⇒ \dfrac{2cos2x}{2}dx = dt$

$⇒ y \cdot {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)} = ∫ {e}^{- t}dt + c$

$⇒ y \cdot {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)} = - {e}^{- t}dt + c$

$⇒ y \cdot {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)} = - {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)} + c$

Given, $y\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = 0$

$⇒ 0 \cdot {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}{2}\right)} = - {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)}{2}\right)} + c$

$⇒ c = - {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}$

$⇒ y \cdot {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)} = - {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{2}\right)} + {e}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}$

Now, at $x = 0$

$⇒ y\left(0\right) \cdot {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin0}{2}\right)} = - {e}^{- \left(\dfrac{sin0}{2}\right)} + {e}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}$

$⇒ y\left(0\right) \cdot {e}^{0} = - {e}^{0} + {e}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}$

$⇒ y\left(0\right) = - 1 + {e}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}$

$⇒ y\left(0\right) + 1 = {e}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}$

$⇒ {\left(y\left(0\right) + 1\right)}^{2} = {e}^{- 1} .$

36822.subject: Mathematics
36822.text: Let $a, b, c \in \{1, 2, 3, 4\}$. If the probability, that $ax^2 + 2\sqrt{2}\,bx + c > 0$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$, is $\dfrac{m}{n}$, $\gcd(m, n) = 1$, then $m + n$ is equal to _______.
36822.sol:
For the quadratic expression $ax^2 + 2\sqrt{2}bx + c > 0$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$, the leading coefficient must be positive and the discriminant must be negative.

Since $a \in \{1, 2, 3, 4\}$, the condition $a > 0$ is always satisfied.

The discriminant condition is:
$D < 0$
$\Rightarrow (2\sqrt{2}b)^2 - 4ac < 0$
$\Rightarrow 8b^2 - 4ac < 0$
$\Rightarrow 2b^2 < ac$

The total number of possible triplets $(a, b, c)$ is $4 \times 4 \times 4 = 64$.

Now, we find the number of favorable outcomes by checking the possible values of $b \in \{1, 2, 3, 4\}$:

Case 1: $b = 1$
We need $2(1)^2 < ac \Rightarrow ac > 2$.
The total number of pairs $(a, c)$ is $4 \times 4 = 16$.
The pairs for which $ac \le 2$ are $(1, 1), (1, 2), (2, 1)$, which are $3$ in number.
So, the number of pairs with $ac > 2$ is $16 - 3 = 13$.

Case 2: $b = 2$
We need $2(2)^2 < ac \Rightarrow ac > 8$.
The possible pairs $(a, c)$ from the given set are $(3, 3), (3, 4), (4, 3), (4, 4)$.
So, there are $4$ pairs.

Case 3: $b = 3$
We need $2(3)^2 < ac \Rightarrow ac > 18$.
Since the maximum possible value of $ac$ is $4 \times 4 = 16$, there are $0$ pairs.

Case 4: $b = 4$
We need $2(4)^2 < ac \Rightarrow ac > 32$.
Again, there are $0$ pairs.

Total number of favorable outcomes = $13 + 4 = 17$.

The required probability is $\dfrac{m}{n} = \dfrac{17}{64}$.

Since $\gcd(17, 64) = 1$, we have $m = 17$ and $n = 64$.

Therefore, $m + n = 17 + 64 = 81$.

Answer: $81$

37888.subject: Mathematics
37888.text: The square of the distance of the point $(-2, -8, 6)$ from the line $\dfrac{x-1}{1} = \dfrac{y-1}{2} = \dfrac{z}{-1}$ along the line $\dfrac{x+5}{1} = \dfrac{y+5}{-1} = \dfrac{z}{2}$ is equal to:
37888.sol:
Let the given point be $P(-2, -8, 6)$.

The distance is measured along the line $\dfrac{x+5}{1} = \dfrac{y+5}{-1} = \dfrac{z}{2}$, which has direction ratios $(1, -1, 2)$.

The equation of the line passing through $P$ and parallel to this line is:
$\dfrac{x+2}{1} = \dfrac{y+8}{-1} = \dfrac{z-6}{2} = \lambda$

Any point on this line can be written as $Q(\lambda - 2, -\lambda - 8, 2\lambda + 6)$.

Since $Q$ lies on the line $\dfrac{x-1}{1} = \dfrac{y-1}{2} = \dfrac{z}{-1}$, we substitute the coordinates of $Q$ into its equation:
$\dfrac{\lambda - 2 - 1}{1} = \dfrac{-\lambda - 8 - 1}{2} = \dfrac{2\lambda + 6}{-1}$

$\dfrac{\lambda - 3}{1} = \dfrac{-\lambda - 9}{2} = \dfrac{2\lambda + 6}{-1}$

Taking the first two parts:
$2(\lambda - 3) = -\lambda - 9$
$2\lambda - 6 = -\lambda - 9$
$3\lambda = -3 \Rightarrow \lambda = -1$

Substituting $\lambda = -1$ into the coordinates of $Q$, we get:
$Q(-1 - 2, -(-1) - 8, 2(-1) + 6) \equiv Q(-3, -7, 4)$

The square of the distance between $P(-2, -8, 6)$ and $Q(-3, -7, 4)$ is:
$PQ^2 = (-3 - (-2))^2 + (-7 - (-8))^2 + (4 - 6)^2$
$PQ^2 = (-1)^2 + (1)^2 + (-2)^2$
$PQ^2 = 1 + 1 + 4 = 6$

Answer: $6$

39104.text: A parallel plate capacitor has capacitance $C$, when there is vacuum within the parallel plates. Original capacitance: $C = \frac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d}$
After inserting dielectric of thickness $\frac{d}{3}$, system becomes two capacitors in series.

Dielectric region: $C_2 = \frac{K\varepsilon_0 A}{d/3} = 3KC$

$C_{new} = \frac{3KC}{2K+1}$

39655.subject: Physics
39655.text: A $1m$ long wire is broken into two unequal parts $X$ and $Y$. The $X$ part of the wire is stretched into another wire $W$. Length of $W$ is twice the length of $X$ and the resistance of $W$ is twice that of $Y$. Find the ratio of length of $X$ and $Y$.
39655.sol:
​​​​​​​

Resistance of a wire is given by $R = \dfrac{ρL}{A}$, where, $ρ$ is conductivity, $L$ is length of wire and $A$ is cross-sectional area of wire.

For a single wire, $A$ and $ρ$ are constant.

Thus, for parts $X$ and $Y$, resistance, $\dfrac{{R}_{X}}{{R}_{Y}} = \dfrac{{l}_{X}}{{l}_{Y}}$.

When wire is stretched to double of its length, then resistance becomes four times, thus, ${R}_{W} = 4{R}_{X} = 2{R}_{Y}$.

Hence, the ratio is $\dfrac{{R}_{X}}{{R}_{Y}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

So, $\dfrac{{l}_{X}}{{l}_{Y}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

42256.text:
A NCC parade is going at a uniform speed of $9km{h}^{- 1}$ under a mango tree on which a monkey is sitting at a height of $19 . 6m$. At any particular instant, the monkey drops a mango. A cadet will receive the mango whose distance from the tree at time of drop is :
(Given $g = 9 . 8m{s}^{- 2}$)
42256.sol:
If a cadet receives the mango, then the time taken by the mango to fall and the cadet to reach there should be equal.

Time taken by mango to fall $t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}}$.

$⇒ t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \times 19 . 6}{9 . 8}} = 2s$

Therefore, the distance of the cadet from the tree will be, $d = vt$.

$⇒ d = 9 \times \dfrac{5}{18} \times 2 = 5m$

48518.subject: Mathematics
48518.text: The function $f(x)=\log (1+x)-\frac{2 x}{2+x}$ is increasing on
48518.sol:
Given, $f(x)=\log (1+x)-\frac{2 x}{2+x}$
Differentiating the function w.r.t. $x$, we get

$\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(x) & =\frac{1}{(1+x)}(0+1)-2\left[\frac{(2+x) \times 1-x(0+1)}{(2+x)^2}\right]\\
& =\frac{1}{1+x}-2\left[\frac{2+x-x}{(2+x)^2}\right]=\frac{1}{1+x}-\frac{4}{(2+x)^2}\\
& =\frac{(2+x)^2-4(1+x)}{(1+x)(2+x)^2}=\frac{4+x^2+4 x-4-4 x}{(x+1)(x+2)^2}\\
& =\frac{x^2}{(x+1)(x+2)^2}=\left(\frac{x}{x+2}\right)^2 \cdot \frac{1}{(x+1)}
\end{aligned}$ Sign of $f^{\prime}(x)$ depends on the sign of $\frac{1}{(x+1)} \begin{aligned}& f^{\prime}(x)>0 \text{ when }x>-1 \Rightarrow \text{ increasing }\\
& f^{\prime}(x) < 0 \text{ when }x < -1 \Rightarrow \text{ decreasing }
\end{aligned}$ Hence, $f(x)$ is increasing on $(-1, \infty)$.

49655.text: The general solution of the differential equation $x^{2} d y-2 x y d x=x^{4} \cos x d x$ is
49655.sol:
We have,
$\begin{aligned}
x^{2} d y-2 x y d x &=x^{4} \cos x d x \\
\Rightarrow \quad \quad \frac{d y}{d x}-\frac{2}{x} y &=x^{2} \cos x
\end{aligned}$
Comparing with $\frac{d y}{d x}+P y=Q$
Where $P=-\frac{2}{x}$ and $Q=x^{2} \cos x\therefore \quad \text{ IF }=e^{\int \frac{-2}{x} d x}=e^{-2 \log x}=e^{\log \left(\frac{1}{x^{2}}\right)}=\frac{1}{x^{2}}\therefore$ The solution of the given differential
$y \cdot \operatorname{IF}=\int(Q \times \operatorname{IF}) d x+c\Rightarrow y \times \frac{1}{x^{2}}=\int\left(x^{2} \cos x\right)\left(\frac{1}{x^{2}}\right) d x+c\Rightarrow \quad \frac{y}{x^{2}}=\int \cos x+c\Rightarrow \quad \frac{y}{x^{2}}=\sin x+c\Rightarrow \quad y=x^{2} \sin x+c x^{2}$

52499.subject: Physics
52499.text: Two containers ${C}_{1}$ and ${C}_{2}$ of volumes $V$ and $4V$ respectively, hold the same ideal gas and are connected by a thin horizontal tube of negligible volume with a valve which is initially closed. The initial pressures of the gas in ${C}_{1}$ and ${C}_{2}$ are $p$ and $5p$, respectively. Heat baths are employed to maintain the temperatures in the containers at $300K$ and $400K$, respectively. The valve is now opened. Select the correct statement.
options: The gas will flow from the hot container to the cold one and the process is reversible.
The gas will flow from one container to the other till the number of moles in two containers are equal.
A long time after the valve is opened, the pressure in both the containers will be $3p$.
A long time after the valve is opened, number of moles of gas in the hot container will be thrice that of the cold one.
52499.sol:
Let ${n}_{1}$ and ${n}_{2}$ are number of moles of gas present in container ${C}_{1}$ and ${C}_{2}$ respectively, before the value is opened.

Then, using $pV = nRT$.

${n}_{1} = \dfrac{pV}{R\left(300\right)}$

and ${n}_{2} = \dfrac{5p\left(4V\right)}{R\left(400\right)}$

When value is opened gas flows from ${C}_{2}$ to ${C}_{1}$ till pressure in ${C}_{1}$ and ${C}_{2}$ is equal. Let after equalisation of pressure in both ${C}_{1}$ and ${C}_{2}$, its value is ${p}_{0}$,

Then, using $pV = nRT$.

${p}_{0}V = {n}_{1}^{'}R\left(300\right)$ (Container ${C}_{1}$)

and ${p}_{0}4V = {n}_{2}^{'}R\left(400\right)$ (Container ${C}_{2}$)

So, ${n}_{1}^{'} = \dfrac{{p}_{0}V}{R\left(300\right)}$

As no gas is leaked from containers, 

${n}_{1} + {n}_{2} = {n}_{1}^{'}: {n}_{2}^{'}$

$⇒ \dfrac{pV}{R\left(300\right)} + \dfrac{20pV}{R\left(400\right)}$

$= \dfrac{{p}_{0}V}{R\left(300\right)} + \dfrac{4{p}_{0}V}{R\left(400\right)}$

So, $p\left(\dfrac{1}{300} + \dfrac{20}{400}\right) = {p}_{0}\left(\dfrac{1}{300} + \dfrac{4}{400}\right)$

$⇒ 4p = {p}_{0}$

Now, ${n}_{2}^{'}{n}_{1}^{'} = \dfrac{\dfrac{4{p}_{0}V}{R\left(400\right)}}{\dfrac{{p}_{0}V}{R\left(300\right)}} = 3$

Finally number of moles of ${C}_{2}$ is thrice of ${C}_{1}$.

Now, $b^2+c^2=\left(\frac{\sqrt{3} \lambda}{2}\right)^2$+$\left(\frac{\lambda}{2}\right)^2$=$\frac{3 \lambda^2}{a}+\frac{\lambda^2}{4}=$\lambda^2\therefore \quad b^2+c^2=a^2$

55292.subject: Chemistry
55292.text: Which from following is the most stable species?
55292.sol:
Ammonium ion stability depends on three competing factors: the inductive effect of alkyl groups, solvation through hydrogen bonding, and steric hindrance to solvation.

Alkyl groups donate electron density inductively, stabilizing positive charge. Solvation in aqueous environments favors ions with more hydrogens for hydrogen bonding. Steric hindrance from bulky groups reduces solvation effectiveness.

Experimental pKa values for methyl-substituted ammonium ions reveal the stability order:

$\mathrm{pKa}[(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2 \stackrel{+}{\mathrm{N}} \mathrm{H}_2] (10.73) > \mathrm{pKa}[\mathrm{CH}_3 \stackrel{+}{\mathrm{N}} \mathrm{H}_3] (10.64) > \mathrm{pKa}[(\mathrm{CH}_3)_3 \stackrel{+}{\mathrm{N}} \mathrm{H}] (9.80) > \mathrm{pKa}[\mathrm{NH}_4^{+}] (9.25)$

The secondary ammonium ion $\mathrm{R}_2 \stackrel{+}{\mathrm{N}} \mathrm{H}_2$ achieves optimal balance between inductive stabilization (two alkyl groups) and solvation capacity (two hydrogens), with minimal steric interference.

55777.subject: Chemistry
55777.text: Which from the following molecules does not develop intermolecular hydrogen bonding?
55777.sol:
Intermolecular hydrogen bonding requires hydrogen atoms covalently bonded to highly electronegative atoms (F, O, or N) adjacent to atoms with lone electron pairs.

Water ($\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$) features hydrogen-oxygen bonds with oxygen lone pairs, enabling hydrogen bonding.

Ammonia ($\mathrm{NH}_3$) has hydrogen-nitrogen bonds with nitrogen lone pairs, facilitating hydrogen bonding.

Hydrogen fluoride (HF) contains hydrogen-fluorine bonds with fluorine lone pairs, supporting strong hydrogen bonding.

Bromine ($\mathrm{Br}_2$) lacks hydrogen atoms entirely and consists only of bromine-bromine covalent bonds, precluding hydrogen bonding entirely. Intermolecular forces are limited to London dispersion forces.

$\mathrm{Br}_2$ is therefore the only molecule among these that cannot form intermolecular hydrogen bonds.

56813.text: The graphical variation of molar conductivity $(\Lambda)$ against square root of molar concentration $(\sqrt{c})$ of certain electrolyte 'X' is linear with intercept on y axis. Identify X from following.

This linear relationship with a definite y-intercept (\Lambda_m^{}^{\circ}$) is observed only for strong electrolytes.

Weak electrolytes show a steep curve at low concentrations and do not have a linear plot or a well-defined intercept.

Among the given options, \text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$, $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$, and $\text{HCOOH}$ are weak electrolytes.

$\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$ is a salt of a weak acid and a strong base, making it a strong electrolyte.

Therefore, $\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$ will show a linear variation with an intercept on the y-axis.

Answer: $\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$

60203.subject: Mathematics
60203.text: If $f(x) = \log(1 + x) - \dfrac{x}{1+x}$, then the values of $x$ for which $f(x)$ is monotonically increasing and monotonically decreasing are respectively.....
60203.sol:
The given function is $f(x) = \log(1 + x) - \dfrac{x}{1+x}$

The domain of the function is $1 + x > 0 \Rightarrow x > -1$

Differentiating $f(x)$ with respect to $x$:

$f'(x) = \dfrac{1}{1+x} - \dfrac{(1+x) \cdot 1 - x \cdot 1}{(1+x)^2}$

$f'(x) = \dfrac{1}{1+x} - \dfrac{1}{(1+x)^2}$

$f'(x) = \dfrac{1+x-1}{(1+x)^2} = \dfrac{x}{(1+x)^2}$

For $f(x)$ to be monotonically increasing, $f'(x) > 0$

$\dfrac{x}{(1+x)^2} > 0 \Rightarrow x > 0$

Thus, $f(x)$ is monotonically increasing on $(0, \infty)$

For $f(x)$ to be monotonically decreasing, $f'(x) < 0$

$\dfrac{x}{(1+x)^2} < 0 \Rightarrow x < 0$

Considering the domain $x > -1$, $f(x)$ is monotonically decreasing on $(-1, 0)$

The intervals for monotonically increasing and decreasing are $(0, \infty)$ and $(-1, 0)$ respectively.

Answer: $(0, \infty), (-1, 0)$

60211.subject: Mathematics
60211.text: A triangle has two fixed vertices A $(a, 0)$ and B$(0, b)$ . Let its third vertex C is moving along the line $x = y$. If $s$ is the area of triangle ABC, then $\dfrac{ds}{dx} =$
60211.sol:
Let the coordinates of the vertices of the triangle be $A(a, 0)$, $B(0, b)$, and $C(x, x)$ since $C$ lies on the line $y = x$.

The area of the triangle $s$ is given by the determinant formula:

$s = \dfrac{1}{2} \begin{vmatrix} a & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & b & 1 \\ x & x & 1 \end{vmatrix}$

Expanding the determinant along the first row:

$s = \dfrac{1}{2} [a(b - x) - 0 + 1(0 - bx)]$

$s = \dfrac{1}{2} (ab - ax - bx)$

$s = \dfrac{1}{2} [ab - (a + b)x]$

Differentiating $s$ with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{ds}{dx} = \dfrac{d}{dx} \left[ \dfrac{1}{2} (ab - (a + b)x) \right]$

$\dfrac{ds}{dx} = -\left(\dfrac{a + b}{2}\right)$

Answer: $-\left(\dfrac{a + b}{2}\right)$

61413.text: The particular solution of differential equation $\mathrme^{\frac{d y}{d x}}=(x+1), y(0)=3$ is
61413.sol:
$$
\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{e}^{\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} x}}=(x+1) \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{~d} x}=\log (x+1)
\end{aligned}
$$
Integrating on both sides, we get
$$
\begin{aligned}
\int \mathrm{d} y & =\int \log (x+1) \mathrm{d} x+\mathrm{c} \\
\Rightarrow y & =x \log (x+1)-\int \frac{x}{x+1} \mathrm{~d} x+\mathrm{c} \\
& =x \log (x+1)-\int \frac{x+1-1}{x+1} \mathrm{~d} x+\mathrm{c} \\
& =x \log (x+1)-\int\left(1-\frac{1}{x+1}\right) \mathrm{d} x+\mathrm{c} \\
y & =x \log (x+1)-x+\log (x+1)+\mathrm{c} .
\end{aligned}
$$
Since $y(0)=3$, i.e., $y=3$ when $x=0$
$$
\begin{aligned}
& 3=0+\mathrm{c} \Rightarrow \mathrm{c}=3 \\
& y=x \log (x+1)+\log (x+1)-x+3 \\
& y=(x+1) \log (x+1)-x+3
\end{aligned}
$$

62939.text: Simplest form of the following switching circuit is
62939.sol:
Let $p$ represent the switch $S_1$ and $q$ represent the switch $S_2$.

The given switching circuit consists of three parallel branches. The logical expression for the entire circuit is:

$E = (p \land q) \lor (p \land \sim q) \lor (\sim p \land q)$

We can simplify this boolean expression by grouping the first two terms:

$E = [p \land (q \lor \sim q)] \lor (\sim p \land q)$

Since $q \lor \sim q$ is always true (a tautology, denoted as $T$), we have:

$E = (p \land T) \lor (\sim p \land q)$

$E = p \lor (\sim p \land q)$

Applying the distributive law:

$E = (p \lor \sim p) \land (p \lor q)$

Again, since $p \lor \sim p$ is a tautology ($T$):

$E = T \land (p \lor q)$

$E = p \lor q$

This simplified logical expression represents a circuit where switches $S_1$ and $S_2$ are connected in parallel.

Answer:

63609.text:
For the following probability distribution, the standard deviation of the random variable X is
X 2 3 4
P(X=x) 0.2 0.5 0.3
63609.sol:
To compute the standard deviation of $X$, start with the expected value $E(X) = \sum x \cdot P(X=x)$:

$E(X) = 2 \cdot 0.2 + 3 \cdot 0.5 + 4 \cdot 0.3 = 0.4 + 1.5 + 1.2 = 3.1$

Then find $E(X^2) = \sum x^2 \cdot P(X=x)$:

$E(X^2) = 4 \cdot 0.2 + 9 \cdot 0.5 + 16 \cdot 0.3 = 0.8 + 4.5 + 4.8 = 10.1$

The variance is $\operatorname{Var}(X) = E(X^2) - [E(X)]^2$:

$\operatorname{Var}(X) = 10.1 - (3.1)^2 = 10.1 - 9.61 = 0.49$

Standard deviation is its square root:

$\sqrt{0.49} =$0.7$

Among the choices, \frac{1}{7} \approx 0.1428$ is numerically closest, though units are not cubic.

64073.text: If $x=-2+\sqrt{-3}$, then the value of $2 x^4+5 x^3+7 x^2-x+38$ is equal to
64073.sol:
Given $x = -2 + \sqrt{-3} = -2 + i\sqrt{3}$.

To find the minimal polynomial, observe that $x + 2 = i\sqrt{3}$. Squaring both sides yields $(x + 2)^2 = (i\sqrt{3})^2$, which simplifies to $x^2 + 4x + 4 = -3$, giving the quadratic equation $x^2 + 4x + 7 = 0$.

The polynomial $P(x) = 2x^4 + 5x^3 + 7x^2 - x + 38$ is divided by $x^2 + 4x + 7$:

$2x^4 + 5x^3 + 7x^2 - x + 38 = (x^2 + 4x + 7)(2x^2 - 3x + 5) + 3$

Since $x^2 + 4x + 7 = 0$, substitution gives $P(x) = 0 \cdot (2x^2 - 3x + 5) + 3 = 3$.

Final answer: $\boxed{3}$

64078.text: The equation $\mathrme^{\sin x}-\mathrme^{-\sin x}=4$ has _______ solutions.
64078.sol:
$\mathrme^{\sin x}-e^{-\sin x}-4=0$
Let $\mathrme^{\sin x}=y$, then the given equation can be written as $y^2-4 y-1=0 \Rightarrow y=2 \cdot \pm \sqrt{5}$ But the value of $y=\mathrme^{\sin x}$ is always positive, so $\begin{aligned} & y=2+\sqrt{5} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrme^{\sin x}=2+\sqrt{5} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrme^{\sin x}>\mathrm{e} \\ & \Rightarrow \sin x>1 \end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \ldots[\because 2 < \sqrt{5}] \\ & \ldots[\because 2+\sqrt{5}>\mathrm{e}] \end{aligned}$ which is not possible, since $\sin x$ cannot be greater than 1. Hence, no real value of $x$ satisfies the given equation.

64417.text: Direction cosines of the two lines are satisfied by $l+m+n=0$ and $2 m n+3 \ln -5 \operatorname{lm}=0$. Then the angle between these lines is
64417.sol:
The direction cosines $(l, m, n)$ satisfy $l + m + n = 0$ and $2mn + 3ln - 5lm = 0$.

From the first equation, $n = -(l + m)$. Substituting into the second gives:

$2m(-(l + m)) + 3l(-(l + m)) - 5lm = 0$

Simplifying yields $3l^2 + 10lm + 2m^2 = 0$.

Dividing by $m^2$ (for $m \neq 0$) and setting $x = l/m$ produces $3x^2 + 10x + 2 = 0$.

The roots $x_1$ and $x_2$ correspond to the ratios for the two lines. Applying Vieta's formulas:

$x_1 + x_2 = -10/3$, $x_1 x_2 = 2/3$.

The angle $\theta$ between the lines satisfies:

$\cos\theta = l_1 l_2 + m_1 m_2 + n_1 n_2 = 2x_1x_2 + 2 + x_1 + x_2$

Substituting the known sums and products:

$\cos\theta = 2(2/3) + 2 - 10/3 = 0$

Hence $\theta = \pi/2$.

Answer: A

66300.text: In a meter bridge experiment, the balance point is obtained at length '$l_1$' cm from left hand when resistances in the left gap and right gap are $15 \ \Omega$ and $R \ \Omega$ respectively. When the resistance $R$ is shunted with equal resistance the new balance point is at $(1.6\,l_1)$. The resistance $R$ in ohm is
66300.sol:
For a meter bridge, the balance condition is given by $\dfrac{R_1}{R_2} = \dfrac{l}{100 - l}$.

Initially, the resistances are $15 \ \Omega$ and $R \ \Omega$, and the balance point is at $l_1$.

$\dfrac{15}{R} = \dfrac{l_1}{100 - l_1}$

When $R$ is shunted with an equal resistance $R$, the equivalent resistance in the right gap becomes $\dfrac{R \times R}{R + R} = \dfrac{R}{2}$. The new balance point is at $1.6 l_1$.

$\dfrac{15}{\dfrac{R}{2}} = \dfrac{1.6 l_1}{100 - 1.6 l_1}$

$\dfrac{30}{R} = \dfrac{1.6 l_1}{100 - 1.6 l_1}$

Dividing the second equation by the first equation:

$\dfrac{\dfrac{30}{R}}{\dfrac{15}{R}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1.6 l_1}{100 - 1.6 l_1}}{\dfrac{l_1}{100 - l_1}}$

$2 = \dfrac{1.6(100 - l_1)}{100 - 1.6 l_1}$

$200 - 3.2 l_1 = 160 - 1.6 l_1$

$1.6 l_1 = 40 \Rightarrow l_1 = 25$

Substituting $l_1 = 25$ into the first equation:

$\dfrac{15}{R} = \dfrac{25}{100 - 25}$

$\dfrac{15}{R} = \dfrac{25}{75} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

$R = 15 \times 3 = 45 \ \Omega$

Answer: $45$

For a solinoid magnetic field at the center is:
$B=\mu_0\left(\frac{N}{l}\right) I$,
Total magnetic self flux is:
$\phi=B A N=\mu_0\left(\frac{N}{l}\right) I A N$
According to the definition of magnetic flux and coefficient of self induction:
$\phi=L I$
On comparing the above two expressions, the self-induction of a long solenoid is given by
$L=\frac{\mu_0 N^2}{L}$
where, $N=$ number of truns, $L=$ Length and $A=$ cross - sectional area.
Therefore, the self-induction of a long solenoid does not depend upon the current flowing through it.

67028.text: Two-point charges +2 C and +6 C separated by distance ' r ' repel each other with a force of 18 N. If negative charge of 4 C is added to each of these charges, then the force experienced by them is
67028.sol:
The initial charges are $q_1 = +2\text{ C}$ and $q_2 = +6\text{ C}$, separated by distance $r$. The initial repulsive force is $F_1 = 18\text{ N}$.

Using Coulomb's Law, $F_1 = k \frac{|q_1 q_2|}{r^2} = k \frac{12}{r^2}$, giving $18 = k \frac{12}{r^2}$.

Adding $-4\text{ C}$ to each charge yields $q_1' = -2\text{ C}$ and $q_2' = +2\text{ C}$. The new force is $F_2 = k \frac{|(-2)(2)|}{r^2} = k \frac{4}{r^2}$.

Taking the ratio of the forces, $\frac{F_2}{18} = \frac{4}{12} = \frac{1}{3}$, so $F_2 = \frac{18}{3} = 6\text{ N}$. The charges are opposite in sign, resulting in an attractive force.

Pus is a thick, yellowish or greenish opaque liquid produced in infected tissue, consisting of dead white blood cells (primarily neutrophils), cellular debris from damaged tissues, and dead microbes (bacteria or other pathogens). After phagocytosis, these neutrophils die and accumulate along with the destroyed tissue and microbes to form pus.

Answer: dead neutrophils, damaged tissues and dead microbes

In human males, the reproductive system becomes functional at puberty, which occurs around the age of 12-15 years. Spermatogenesis, the process of sperm production, begins at this time and continues continuously throughout the life of the individual. Unlike human females, who experience menopause and a cessation of reproductive capability around the age of 50, males do not have a definitive end to their reproductive function, although the rate of sperm production and testosterone levels may gradually decline with advanced age.

Answer: throughout the life of the individual

71505.subject: Biology
71505.text: Which one of the following is INCORRECT about double fertilization in angiosperms?
options: Syngamy is the fusion of haploid male and female gametes to form a diploid zygote.
Triple fusion involves the fusion of a haploid male gamete with a diploid secondary nucleus.
Both syngamy and triple fusion are generative fertilization.
Both the male gametes participate in double fertilization.
71505.sol:
Double fertilization in angiosperms involves two types of fusions: syngamy and triple fusion.

Syngamy is the fusion of one haploid male gamete with the haploid egg cell to form a diploid zygote. This process is known as generative fertilization.

Triple fusion is the fusion of the second haploid male gamete with the diploid secondary nucleus (formed by the fusion of two polar nuclei) to form a triploid primary endosperm nucleus (PEN). This process is known as vegetative fertilization.

Since triple fusion is vegetative fertilization and not generative fertilization, the statement claiming both are generative fertilization is incorrect.

Both male gametes participate in these two fusions, making the fourth statement correct.

Answer: Both syngamy and triple fusion are generative fertilization.

77302.text:
For the following two (02) items:
Consider the function $f(x) = \dfrac{x}{1 - x}$ (x > 0$, $x \neq 1$).

What is $(1 - $x)f(\sqrt{x}) +xf(\sqrt{x} +$1)$ equal to?$
77302.sol:
Given $f(x) = \dfrac{x}{1 - x}$

Substitute $\sqrt{x}$ in f(x):

$f(\sqrt{x}) = \dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{1 - \sqrt{x}}$

Substitute $\sqrt{x} + 1$ in f(x):

$f(\sqrt{x} + 1) = \dfrac{\sqrt{x} + 1}{1 - (\sqrt{x} + 1)} = \dfrac{\sqrt{x} + 1}{-\sqrt{x}}$

Now, evaluate the given expression:

$(1 - x)f(\sqrt{x}) + xf(\sqrt{x} + 1) = (1 - x) \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{1 - \sqrt{x}}\right) +$ x$\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{x} + 1}{-\sqrt{x}}\right)

Using 1 - x = (1 - \sqrt{x})(1 + \sqrt{x}):

$= (1 - $\sqrt{x})(1 + \sqrt{x})\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{x}}{1 - \sqrt{x}}\right) - \sqrt{x}(\sqrt{x} +1)$

$= \sqrt{x}(1 + \sqrt{x}) - \sqrt{x}(\sqrt{x} +1)$

$= 0$

Answer: $0$

78508.subject: Mathematics
78508.text:
Given that $\log _x y, \log _z x, \log _y z$ are in GP, $x y z=64$ and $x^3$, $y^3, z^3$ are in A.P.
Which one of the following is correct? $x, y$ and $z$ are
options: neither in AP nor in GP
78508.sol:
Given $\log _x y, \log _z x, \log _y z$ are in G.P.
$\begin{aligned}
& \therefore\left(\log _z x\right)^2=\left(\log _x y\right)\left(\log _y z\right) \\
& \left(\frac{\log x}{\log z}\right)^2=\left(\frac{\log y}{\log x}\right)\left(\frac{\log z}{\log y}\right)=\frac{\log z}{\log x} \\
& \Rightarrow\left(\frac{\log x}{\log z}\right)^3=1 \\
& \Rightarrow \log x=\log z \Rightarrow x=z
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& \because x y z=64 \\
& y=\frac{64}{x^2}
\end{aligned}$
Also given $x^3, y^3 and z^3$ are in A.P.
$\therefore y^3=\frac{x^3+z^3}{2}=\frac{x^3+x^3}{2}\begin{aligned}
& y^3=x^3 \Rightarrow y=x \\
& \Rightarrow x=y=z \\
& x \cdot y \cdot z=64 \\
& x=y=z=4
\end{aligned}$
Thus $x, y, z$ are in A.P. and G.P. both.

78686.text: What is the variance of the first 11 natural numbers?

Variance : The square of standard deviation is called the variance $\left(\sigma^2\right)\therefore \quad \sigma^2=\frac{\Sigma(x-\overline{\mathrm{X}})^2}{n},$
where $\overline{\mathrm{X}}=$ mean of given data
$\bar{x}=$ mean of 1st eleven natural numbers.
$=\frac{11 \times 12}{2 \times 11}=6\therefore \sigma^2=\frac{(1-6)^2+(2-6)^2+(3-6)^2+\ldots \ldots+(11-6)^2}{11}=\frac{2\left[1^2+2^2+3^2+4^2+5^2\right]}{11}=\frac{2 \times 5 \times 6 \times 11}{11 \times 6}=10$.

80175.subject: Botany
80175.text: Which of the following is not a product of a light reaction of photosynthesis?
80175.sol:
NADH is not a product of the light reaction of photosynthesis.NAD (nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide) and NADP (nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate) are the most abundant types of coenzymes inside the cell which are used as electron and hydrogen carriers. NADH and NADPH are the reduced forms of NAD and NADP, respectively. Though NADH and NADPH are structurally more similar, they differ by their role in the cell. The main difference between NADH and NADPH is that NADH is used in cellular respiration, whereas NADPH is used in photosynthesis. NADH is produced in the glycolysis and Krebs cycle and is used in the electron transport chain to produce ATP via oxidative phosphorylation.

NADPH is produced in the light reaction of photosynthesis and is used in the Calvin cycle to assimilate carbon dioxide. ATPs are produced during photophosphorylation, and oxygen is evolved during the photolysis of water.

80414.sol: Oxidative phosphorylation uses the energy of oxidation-reduction of a substrate to generate ATP. Oxidative phosphorylation is made up of two closely connected components: the electron transport chain and chemiosmosis. In chemiosmosis, the energy stored in the gradient is used to make ATP.

83998.sol:
Bacitlus thuringiensis is a Gram-positive, soil dwelling bacterium, also occurs naturally in the gut of caterpillars of various types of moths and butterflies.
During sporulation, B. thuringiensis forms crystals of proteinaceous insecticidal by cry genes. It was determined that the oy genes are harbored in the plasmids of $B$. thuringiensis strains. Cry toxins have specific activities against species of the orderLepidoptera (moths and butterflies), Diptera (flies and mosquitoes) and Coleoptera (beetles). Thus, $B$. thuringiensis serves as an important reservoir of cry toxins and cry genes for the production of biological insecticides and insect resistant genetically modified crops.

84058.subject: Zoology
84058.text: Which of the following conditions cause erythroblastosis foetalis?
84058.sol:
A special case of $Rh$ incompatibility (mismatching) has been observed between the ${Rh}^{- ve}$ blood of a pregnant mother with ${Rh}^{+ ve}$ blood of the foetus. The ${Rh}^{- ve}$ mother is not usually exposed to the $Rh$ antigen of the foetus during the first pregnancy as the foetal and maternal blood are normally kept well separated by the placental barriers. However, at the time of the birth of the first child, there is a possibility of exposure of the maternal blood to a small amount of ${Rh}^{+ ve}$ blood from the foetus. Hence, the body of the mother starts preparing antibodies against $Rh$ antigens in her blood.

These antibodies (a type of $IgG$ antibody) could cross the placental barriers in subsequent pregnancies and cause haemolysis of the ${Rh}^{+ ve}$ red blood cells of the foetus. This could be fatal to the foetus or could cause severe anaemia and jaundice to the baby ($HDN$- a haemolytic disease of newly born). This condition is called erythroblastosis fetalis.

85092.sol: Amensalism is any relationship between organisms of different species in which one organism is inhibited or destroyed while the other organism remains unaffected. It is a type of ecological interaction. A very prominent example of ammensalism is observed during the production of antibiotics. The production of penicillin by Penicillium on a nutrient agar medium shows a zone of inhibition in which other microbes cannot grow. This interaction is also called antibiosis, in which Penicillium gains nothing but adversely affects other microbes.

86067.subject: Chemistry
86067.text: The increasing order of acidic strength for the aqua complexes $[\text{V(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+}$, $[\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+}$, $[\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$, and $[\text{Co(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$ is:
86067.sol:
The acidic strength of an aqua complex is determined by the polarizing power of the central metal ion, which is directly proportional to its charge and inversely proportional to its ionic radius (charge-to-size ratio).

Higher oxidation states lead to a greater charge density. Therefore, the $+3$ metal ions ($\text{Fe}^{3+}$, $\text{Co}^{3+}$) have a significantly higher polarizing power than the $+2$ metal ions ($\textV^{2+}$, $\text{Fe}^{2+}$). This makes the $+3$ aqua complexes more acidic than the $+2$ aqua complexes.

For the $+2$ ions, as we move from left to right across the 3d transition series, the effective nuclear charge increases and the ionic radius generally decreases. The ionic radius of $\textV^{2+}$ is larger than that of $\text{Fe}^{2+}$. Consequently, $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ has a higher polarizing power, making $[\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+}$ more acidic than $[\text{V(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+}$.

Similarly, for the $+3$ ions, the ionic radius of $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ is larger than that of $\text{Co}^{3+}$. The smaller size of $\text{Co}^{3+}$ gives it a higher polarizing power, making $[\text{Co(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$ more acidic than $[\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$.

Combining these factors, the increasing order of acidic strength is:

$[\text{V(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+} < [\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+} < [\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+} < [\text{Co(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$

Answer: $[\text{V(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+} < [\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+} < [\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+} < [\text{Co(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$

88743.text: What will be the pH of a solution formed by mixing 40 $cm^{3}$ of 0.1 M HCl with 10 $cm^{3}$ of 0.45 M NaOH?
88743.sol:
Number of moles of HCl $= \dfrac{MV}{1000} = \dfrac{0.1 \times 40}{1000} = 0.004$
Number of moles of NaOH $= \dfrac{MV}{1000} = \dfrac{0.45 \times 10}{1000} = 0.0045$
Remaining moles of NaOH after neutralization = 0.0045 – 0.004 = 0.0005
Molarity of $OH^{-}= \dfrac{0.0005}{50} \times 1000 = 0.01\text{M}$
So pOH $= 2$
So pH = 14 – 2 = 12

A spring of force constant $k$ and natural length $l$ is attached at $A$ and its other end is attached to a small bead of mass $m$. The bead can slide without friction on the rod. 93471.sol:
Velocity will be maximum at the equilibrium position

$⇒ kx = m{\omega}^{2}\left(l + x\right)$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{m{\omega}^{2}l}{k - m{\omega}^{2}}$

Now, using work-energy theorem

    

$∆ KE =$ Work done by all the forces

$\dfrac{1}{2}m{V}_{\text{max}}^{2} = {∫}_{0}^{x}m{\omega}^{2}\left(l + x\right)dx - \dfrac{1}{2}k{x}^{2}$

$⇒ {V}_{\text{max}}^{2} = \dfrac{2m{\omega}^{2}lx + m{\omega}^{2}{x}^{2} - k{x}^{2}}{m}$

${V}_{\text{max}}^{2} = \dfrac{\left(m{\omega}^{2}l + m{\omega}^{2}\left(l + x\right) - kx\right)x}{m}$

$= \dfrac{m{\omega}^{2}lx}{m}$

$⇒ {V}_{\text{max}}^{2} = {\omega}^{2}lx = \dfrac{m{\omega}^{4}{l}^{2}}{k - m{\omega}^{2}}$

${V}_{\text{max}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{m{\omega}^{4}{l}^{2}}{k - m{\omega}^{2}}}$

101041.subject: Physics
101041.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
101041.text: A ball of mass $0.3 \text{ kg}$ strikes a rigid vertical wall with a speed of $10 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ at an angle of $30^\circ$ with the surface of the wall. It rebounds with the same speed and at the same angle. The magnitude of the impulse imparted to the ball by the wall is:
101041.sol:
Let the wall be along the y-axis and the normal to the wall be along the x-axis.

The angle made by the velocity vector with the surface of the wall is $\theta = 30^\circ$.

The component of velocity perpendicular to the wall is $v_{\perp} = v \sin 30^\circ$.
The component of velocity parallel to the wall is $v_{\parallel} = v \cos 30^\circ$.

During the collision, the parallel component remains unchanged, while the perpendicular component reverses its direction.

Initial momentum perpendicular to the wall, $p_{i} = m v \sin 30^\circ$
Final momentum perpendicular to the wall, $p_{f} = -m v \sin 30^\circ$

Magnitude of impulse = Change in momentum = $|p_{f} - p_{i}| = 2 m v \sin 30^\circ$

Impulse $= 2 \times 0.3 \times 10 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 3 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$.

Answer: $3 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$

101702.subject: Physics
101702.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Two spheres of the same material and radii $R$ and $2R$ fall through the same viscous liquid. When they attain their respective terminal velocities, the ratio of the viscous drag forces on them is $1 : 8$.

Reason (R): The viscous drag force on a sphere moving at its terminal velocity is directly proportional to the cube of its radius.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
101702.sol:
According to Stokes' law, the viscous drag force is given by $F_v = 6\pi\eta r v$.

The terminal velocity $v_t$ of a sphere of radius $r$ and density $\rho$ falling in a liquid of density $\sigma$ and viscosity $\eta$ is given by $v_t = \dfrac{2}{9}\dfrac{r^2(\rho - \sigma)g}{\eta}$.

Therefore, the terminal velocity is directly proportional to the square of the radius ($v_t \propto r^2$).

Substituting this into Stokes' law, we get $F_v \propto r(r^2) \Rightarrow F_v \propto r^3$.

Thus, the Reason is correct.

For two spheres of radii $R$ and $2R$, the ratio of their viscous drag forces at terminal velocity will be $R^3 : (2R)^3 = 1 : 8$.

Thus, the Assertion is also correct, and the Reason is the correct explanation for the Assertion.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

102241.text: At $-73\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$, the root mean square (rms) speed of Helium gas molecules is $v$. At what temperature will the rms speed of Hydrogen gas molecules be $100\%$ more than $v$?
102241.sol:
The rms speed of a gas is given by $v = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$.

For Helium ($M_{\text{He}} = 4\ \text{g/mol}$):
Initial temperature, $T_{\text{He}} = -73 + 273 = 200\ \text{K}$
$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{3R(200)}{4}} = \sqrt{150R}$

For Hydrogen ($M_{\text{H}_2} = 2\ \text{g/mol}$):
The target speed is $100\%$ more than $v$, which means the new speed is $v + v = 2v$.
$v_{\text{H}_2} = 2v = 2\sqrt{150R} = \sqrt{4 \times 150R} = \sqrt{600R}$

Equating this to the formula for Hydrogen's rms speed:
$\sqrt{\dfrac{3RT_{\text{H}_2}}{2}} = \sqrt{600R}$

Squaring both sides:
$\dfrac{3T_{\text{H}_2}}{2} = 600$

$T_{\text{H}_2} = \dfrac{600 \times 2}{3} = 400\ \text{K}$

Converting back to Celsius:
$T_{\text{H}_2} = 400 - 273 = 127\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$

Answer: $127\ ^{\circ}\text{C}$

102469.subject: Physics
102469.text: Two identical blocks of mass $m$ are attached to two separate ideal springs having force constants $16k$ and $9k$. The blocks are displaced from their mean positions and released simultaneously in the same phase. What is the minimum number of oscillations completed by the block attached to the $16k$ spring when both blocks are in the same phase again at their mean position?
102469.sol:
The time period of a spring-mass system is given by $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{K}}$.

For the two systems, the masses are identical, so the time period depends only on the force constant as $T \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{K}}$.

Let $T_1$ be the time period of the block on the $16k$ spring and $T_2$ be the time period of the block on the $9k$ spring.

$\dfrac{T_1}{T_2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{9k}{16k}} = \dfrac{3}{4}$

This implies $4T_1 = 3T_2$.

Both blocks will be in the same phase again at their mean position when the time elapsed is a common multiple of their time periods. The minimum time for this to happen is $t = 4T_1 = 3T_2$.

Therefore, the block attached to the $16k$ spring (which has the shorter time period and oscillates faster) completes $4$ oscillations.

Answer: $4$

102646.text:
Match List-I with List-II for organ pipes of length $L$.

List-I (Mode of vibration)List-II (Wavelength $\lambda$)
(A) Fundamental mode of a closed pipe(I) $L$
(B) Fundamental mode of an open pipe(II) $\dfrac{4L}{3}$
(C) First overtone of a closed pipe(III) $2L$
(D) First overtone of an open pipe(IV) $4L$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
102646.sol:
For a closed pipe of length $L$, the allowed wavelengths are given by $L = \dfrac{n\lambda}{4}$ where $n = 1, 3, 5, \dots$
For the fundamental mode ($n = 1$), $\lambda = 4L$.
For the first overtone ($n = 3$), $\lambda = \dfrac{4L}{3}$.

For an open pipe of length $L$, the allowed wavelengths are given by $L = \dfrac{n\lambda}{2}$ where $n = 1, 2, 3, \dots$
For the fundamental mode ($n = 1$), $\lambda = 2L$.
For the first overtone ($n = 2$), $\lambda = L$.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)

102790.text:
Statement-I : The electric potential and the electric field intensity at the centre of a square having four point charges at their vertices (as shown) are zero.
Statement-II : Electric field is negative derivative of the potential.
options: Statement-I is True, Statement-II is True; Statement-II is a correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is True, Statement-II is True; Statement-II is NOT a correct explanation for Statement-1
Statement-I is True, Statement-II is False
Statement-I is False, Statement-II is True.
102790.sol:
- Statement-I: The electric potential and the electric field intensity at the center of a square having four point charges \(+q,-q,-q,+q\) at their vertices are not zero. Although the electric field at the center due to the symmetry of opposite charges might cancel out, the potential at the center is not zero. The potential is a scalar quantity and doesn't cancel like vectors (it adds algebraically), so the total potential is not zero.
- Statement-II: The electric field is indeed the negative derivative of the electric potential. This is a fundamental relationship in electrostatics:
\(\mathrm{E}=-\nabla V\)
Therefore, Statement-I is False and Statement-II is True.

103676.subject: Physics
103676.text: A straight steel wire of length $L$ acts as a magnet with a magnetic moment $M$. It is then bent at its midpoint such that its new magnetic moment becomes $\dfrac{\sqrt{3}M}{2}$. The angle between the two arms of the bent wire is:
103676.sol:
The initial magnetic moment of the straight wire is $M = m \times L$, where $m$ is the pole strength.

When the wire is bent at its midpoint, it forms two arms, each of length $\dfrac{L}{2}$, with an angle $\theta$ between them. The new effective length $L'$ is the straight-line distance between the two ends.

Using the cosine rule for the triangle formed by the two arms and the distance between the ends:
$(L')^2 = \left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right)^2 + \left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right)^2 - 2\left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right)\left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right)\cos\theta$
$(L')^2 = \dfrac{L^2}{4} + \dfrac{L^2}{4} - \dfrac{L^2}{2}\cos\theta = \dfrac{L^2}{2}(1 - \cos\theta)$

The new magnetic moment is given as $M' = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}M}{2}$. Since $M' = m \times L'$ and $M = m \times L$, we have:
$L' = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}L}{2}$

Substituting $L'$ into the cosine rule equation:
$\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}L}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{L^2}{2}(1 - \cos\theta)$
$\dfrac{3L^2}{4} = \dfrac{L^2}{2}(1 - \cos\theta)$
$\dfrac{3}{2} = 1 - \cos\theta$
$\cos\theta = 1 - \dfrac{3}{2} = -\dfrac{1}{2}$

The angle whose cosine is $-\dfrac{1}{2}$ is $\theta = 120^{\circ}$.

Alternatively, using the direct formula for a magnet bent at its midpoint: $M' = M \sin\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)$.
$\dfrac{\sqrt{3}M}{2} = M \sin\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right) \Rightarrow \sin\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \Rightarrow \dfrac{\theta}{2} = 60^{\circ} \Rightarrow \theta = 120^{\circ}$.

Answer: $120^{\circ}$

104870.subject: Physics
104870.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The kinetic energy of an electron in the first excited state of a hydrogen atom is four times its kinetic energy in the third excited state.

Reason (R): The kinetic energy of an electron in a hydrogen atom is inversely proportional to the square of the principal quantum number.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
104870.sol:
Reason (R) is correct: According to Bohr's model, the kinetic energy of an electron in the $n^{\text{th}}$ orbit of a hydrogen atom is $K = \dfrac{13.6}{n^2} \text{ eV}$. Thus, $K \propto \dfrac{1}{n^2}$.

Assertion (A) is correct: The first excited state corresponds to the principal quantum number $n_1 = 2$, and the third excited state corresponds to $n_2 = 4$.

Using the relation from the Reason:
$K_1 \propto \dfrac{1}{2^2} = \dfrac{1}{4}$
$K_2 \propto \dfrac{1}{4^2} = \dfrac{1}{16}$

The ratio of their kinetic energies is $\dfrac{K_1}{K_2} = \dfrac{1/4}{1/16} = 4$.
Therefore, the kinetic energy in the first excited state is four times that in the third excited state.

Since the inverse-square relationship directly leads to the calculated ratio, (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

104997.subject: Physics
104997.text:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the dependence of nuclear properties on mass number $A$.

List-IList-II
A. Nuclear RadiusI. Independent of $A$
B. Nuclear VolumeII. Proportional to $A^{1/3}$
C. Nuclear DensityIII. Proportional to $A$
D. Nuclear MassIV. Proportional to $A^{-1/3}$


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A - II, B - III, C - I, D - III
A - II, B - II, C - III, D - I
A - III, B - II, C - I, D - II
A - II, B - III, C - III, D - I
104997.sol:
The radius of a nucleus is given by $R = R_0 A^{1/3}$. Thus, nuclear radius is proportional to $A^{1/3}$ (A matches to II).

The volume of the nucleus is $V = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi R^3 = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi R_0^3 A$. Thus, nuclear volume is proportional to $A$ (B matches to III).

Nuclear density is the ratio of nuclear mass to nuclear volume. Since both mass and volume are approximately proportional to $A$, nuclear density is independent of $A$ (C matches to I).

The mass of a nucleus is approximately equal to $A$ times the mass of a nucleon. Thus, nuclear mass is approximately proportional to $A$ (D matches to III).

Therefore, the correct matching is A - II, B - III, C - I, D - III.

Answer: A - II, B - III, C - I, D - III

105785.text:

Statement-I : \(2 \mathrm{~A}+3 \mathrm{~B} \rightarrow \mathrm{C}\)
\(\frac{4}{3}\) moles of ' \(C\) ' are produced when 3 moles of ' \(A\) ' and 4 moles of ' \(B\) ' are added.
Statement-II : 'A' is limiting reagent for the given data.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Statement-I and II both are correct.
Statement-I is correct while II is incorrect.
Both Statement-I and II are incorrect.

105785.sol:
Statement-I:
"4/3 moles of 'C' are produced when 3 moles of ' \(A\) ' and 4 moles of ' \(B\) ' are added."
- From the balanced equation, 2 moles of \(A\) require 3 moles of \(B\).
- We have 3 moles of \(A\), so 4.5 moles of \(B\) are required, but only 4 moles of \(B\) are available.
- \(B\) is the limiting reagent.
- Using 4 moles of B , the moles of C produced:
\(\frac{1}{3} \times 4=\frac{4}{3}\) moles of C.
Statement-II:
" A is the limiting reagent for the given data."
Since B is the limiting reagent, Statement-II is incorrect.

106981.subject: Chemistry
106981.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
106981.text:
Four elements $\mathrm{A}$, $\mathrm{B}$, $\mathrm{C}$, and $\mathrm{D}$ belong to the same short period of the periodic table. The sudden large jump in their successive ionization enthalpies occurs as follows:
Element $\mathrm{A}$: between $\Delta_{i}H_{1}$ and $\Delta_{i}H_{2}$
Element $\mathrm{B}$: between $\Delta_{i}H_{2}$ and $\Delta_{i}H_{3}$
Element $\mathrm{C}$: between $\Delta_{i}H_{3}$ and $\Delta_{i}H_{4}$
Element $\mathrm{D}$: between $\Delta_{i}H_{5}$ and $\Delta_{i}H_{6}$

Which of these elements is expected to form the most acidic oxide?
106981.sol:
The position of the massive jump in successive ionization enthalpies indicates the number of valence electrons an element possesses.

For element $\mathrm{A}$, the jump is after the first electron, meaning it has $1$ valence electron (Group 1).
For element $\mathrm{B}$, the jump is after the second electron, meaning it has $2$ valence electrons (Group 2).
For element $\mathrm{C}$, the jump is after the third electron, meaning it has $3$ valence electrons (Group 13).
For element $\mathrm{D}$, the jump is after the fifth electron, meaning it has $5$ valence electrons (Group 15).

Across a period from left to right, the non-metallic character of elements increases. Since non-metal oxides are acidic in nature, the acidic character of the oxides increases across a period. Element $\mathrm{D}$ (Group 15) is the most non-metallic among the given elements and will therefore form the most acidic oxide.

Answer: Element $\mathrm{D}$

107558.subject: Chemistry
107558.text:
Observe the following statements
i. The dipole moment of $\mathrm{NH}_3$ is higher than the dipole moment of $\mathrm{NF}_3$.
ii. The dipole moment of chloroform is zero.
iii. Covalent bond character in $\mathrm{NaCl}$ is more compared to $\mathrm{CuCl}$.
107558.sol:
Only statement (i) is correct.
- i. The dipole moment of \(\mathrm{NH}_3\) is higher than the dipole moment of \(\mathrm{NF}_3\). This is correct. In \(\mathrm{NH}_3\), the bond dipoles of the three \(\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{H}\) bonds and the lone pair on nitrogen all point in the same general direction, adding up to a larger net dipole moment. In \(N F_3\), the bond dipoles of the three N-F bonds point towards the highly electronegative fluorine atoms, while the lone pair dipole points away. These dipoles oppose each other, resulting in a much smaller net dipole moment.
- if. The dipole moment of chloroform is zero. This is incorrect. Chloroform (\(\mathrm{CHCl}_3\)) is a tetrahedral molecule with three highly electronegative chlorine atoms and one less electronegative hydrogen atom. The bond dipoles do not cancel each other out, resulting in a significant net dipole moment.
- iii. Covalent bond character in NaCl is more compared to CuCl . This is incorrect. According to Fajan's rules, a smaller cation with a pseudo-noble gas configuration (like \(C u^{+}\)) has a greater polarizing power than a cation with a noble gas configuration (like \(\mathrm{Na}^{+}\)). This increased polarizing power leads to a greater covalent character. Therefore, CuCl is more covalent than NaCl.

111908.text: In order to detect elements such as nitrogen, sulphur, and halogens in an organic compound, their covalent bonds must be broken to convert them into water-soluble ionic species. 111908.sol:
In qualitative analysis of organic compounds, elements like nitrogen, sulphur, and halogens are covalently bonded. To detect them, they must be converted into their ionic forms.

This is achieved by fusing the organic compound with sodium metal, a process known as sodium fusion or Lassaigne's test. The covalent compounds are converted into water-soluble ionic sodium salts (such as $\text{NaCN}$, $\text{Na}_2\text{S}$, and $\text{NaX}$).

Kjeldahl's and Dumas methods are used for the quantitative estimation of nitrogen, while the Carius method is used for the quantitative estimation of halogens and sulphur.

Answer: Sodium fusion (Lassaigne's test)

118796.subject: Chemistry
118796.text: An alkene 'A' undergoes acid-catalysed hydration to yield a major product 'B'. When 'B' is treated with Lucas reagent, it produces immediate turbidity at room temperature. Identify the alkene 'A'.
118796.sol:
The production of immediate turbidity with Lucas reagent (concentrated $\mathrm{HCl}$ and anhydrous $\mathrm{ZnCl_2}$) at room temperature is a characteristic test for tertiary alcohols. Therefore, the major product 'B' must be a tertiary alcohol.

Acid-catalysed hydration of alkenes follows Markovnikov's rule, where the $\mathrm{OH}$ group attaches to the more substituted carbon atom of the double bond.

Let us evaluate the hydration products of the given alkenes:
Propene yields propan-2-ol (a secondary alcohol).
But-1-ene yields butan-2-ol (a secondary alcohol).
Ethene yields ethanol (a primary alcohol).
2-Methylpropene yields 2-methylpropan-2-ol (a tertiary alcohol).

Since 2-methylpropan-2-ol is a tertiary alcohol, it will give immediate turbidity with Lucas reagent. Thus, the starting alkene 'A' is 2-methylpropene.

Answer: 2-Methylpropene

125958.subject: Botany
125958.text: How many cotyledons do monocotyledonous embryos possess?
125958.sol: Embryo develops at the micropylar end of the embryo sac where the zygote is situated. Most zygotes divide only after certain amount of endosperm is formed. The portion of embryonal axis above the level of cotyledons is the epicotyl, which terminates with the plumule or stem tip. The cylindrical portion below the level of cotyledons is hypocotyl that terminates at its lower end in the radicle or root tip. The root tip is covered with a root cap. Embryos of monocotyledons possess only one cotyledon. In the grass family the cotyledon is called scutellum that is situated towards one side (lateral) of the embryonal axis. At its lower end, the embryonal axis has theradical and root cap enclosed in an undifferentiated sheath called coleorrhiza. The portion of the embryonal axis above the level of attachment of scutellum is the epicotyl. Epicotyl has a shoot apex and a few leaf primordia enclosed in a hollow foliar structure, the coleoptile.

126209.subject: Botany
126209.text: If the microspore mother cell of a beet plant contains 18 chromosomes, what will be the number of chromosomes in the cells of its perisperm and endosperm, respectively?
126209.sol:
The microspore mother cell (MMC) is a diploid cell ($2n$). Given $2n = 18$, the haploid chromosome number ($n$) is 9.

Perisperm is the residual persistent nucellus, which is a maternal diploid tissue. Thus, the ploidy of perisperm is $2n$, and its cells will contain 18 chromosomes.

The endosperm in angiosperms develops from the primary endosperm nucleus (PEN) formed by triple fusion. Thus, its ploidy is $3n$, and its cells will contain $3 \times 9 = 27$ chromosomes.

Therefore, the correct pair is 18 and 27.

Answer: 18 and 27

Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
128156.sol:
Assertion (A) is true because glands that secrete earwax, milk, and digestive enzymes are exocrine glands. Exocrine glands release their secretions through ducts or tubes.
